message.content:
### Quick Check (Command Prompt)

Open **Command Prompt** (or PowerShell) and type:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"
```

If VS Code is running you’ll see an entry like:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
Code.exe                    12345 Console                    1     200,000 K
```

If it’s not running you’ll get:

```
INFO: No tasks are running which match the specified criteria.
```

---

### Using PowerShell (more convenient)

```powershell
Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

If the process exists it will list its details; otherwise nothing will be returned.

---

### One‑liner to exit with a success/failure status

If you want to use this in a batch file or script and have it return a non‑zero exit code when VS Code isn’t running:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe" | findstr /I "Code.exe" >nul
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo VS Code is NOT running
    exit /b 1
) else (
    echo VS Code is running
    exit /b 0
)
```

---

### How to use the `functions.cmd_controller_execute` tool

If you’d like me to actually run the command on your machine (assuming you’re on Windows), I can do so via the provided tool. Just let me know and I’ll execute:

```json
{
  "command": "tasklist /FI \"IMAGENAME eq Code.exe\""
}
```

(You can replace the command string with any other Windows command you need.)
